notes: The photo reader learns what the reply path already knew. There are two roads to the vision endpoint: the reply itself, which got health-aware waiting and lost-job resubmission last build, and the quick photo-describe job behind every "looking at your photo" — which was still a flat 45-poll loop that gave up 2¼ minutes into a cold boot and swallowed every failure without a word. That silence was the log's unexplained "couldn't read your photo". The reader now plays by the same rules as replies: a rejected submission logs the HTTP status and body, a FAILED job logs its error message, the wait extends a minute at a time while a worker is genuinely booting (up to ten), it fails fast with a pointed message when RunPod can't start any worker at all, and when the job shows the lost-job signature — workers idle, queue empty, nothing in progress, twice in a row — it cancels and resubmits once, which an idle worker picks up in seconds. A connection that stays dead for a full minute of polls ends the attempt instead of spinning forever. Every give-up now names its reason in the log, so the next "couldn't read your photo" comes with a diagnosis attached instead of a shrug.
